name: Paarai
overview: Paarai was a male warrior known as the Arbite and recognized as the thirtieth member of "the thirty," an elite group of David's mighty men. While his tribal affiliation is not recorded, his inclusion among David's men highlights his role in the king's military exploits. No additional personal notes are provided about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Paarai means "devotee of Peor," indicating a proper name with a specific meaning, though it was not given by God. He is also referred to as Naarai, meaning "young man of YHWH," showing a variant name with a distinct meaning in Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Paarai was the father of Ezbai, establishing a direct familial relationship. Beyond this, no further family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Paarai's significance lies in his role as one of David's mighty men, specifically as the thirtieth in this distinguished group, which underscores his valor and loyalty in service to King David. His identification as the Arbite situates him geographically and culturally within the broader narrative of Israel's history. Through his son Ezbai, his legacy continued within the community associated with David's reign.
